head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): S2a — truncate lease lock before rewrite + sanitize empty owner (#9358)

Campaign 81f9be4b attempt-5 lock corruption: open-output-file 'can-update
does NOT truncate, so file-position 0 + write left a stale tail from the
previous (longer) owner — observed: . The lease file became
unreadable, defeating D4 owner diagnostics. The re-dispatch path also
wrote (owner . ""), so a stale lease could not be attributed.

Fix:
- file-truncate port 0 before rewriting the lease.
- Sanitize owner: empty/missing session-id falls back to "unknown".
- campaign-lease records the sanitized owner.

Tests: test-gsd-go-orchestrator.rkt +2 — stale-tail truncation regression
(previous longer owner must not leave fragments) and empty-owner
sanitization.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(gsd): D8 — campaign-aware provider retry + infra-meta-fix without attempt consumption (#9357)

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): D8 — campaign-aware provider retry + infra-meta-fix without attempt consumption (#9357)

Campaign 81f9be4b W3 attempt-4: 30/30 tool calls completed, then ONE
transient 120 s SSE read timeout → progressive-stall circuit break →
turn error → wave-failed, attempt consumed. The executor inherited the
interactive provider-retry policy (max-retries 2, stall-breaker 2,
300 s ceiling) against a 1800 s wave budget.

(A) Campaign-aware retry scaling:
- runtime/provider-retry.rkt: current-provider-retry-max-retries /
  stall-max-consecutive / ceiling-secs parameters (defaults unchanged
  for interactive turns); call-with-provider-retry reads them.
- execute-campaign-request! parameterizes them to wave scale: 5 retries,
  4-stall tolerance, ceiling = min(900, wave-timeout/2).

(B) Infra-meta-fix without attempt consumption:
- infra-failure? classifier (go-orchestrator): classify-error domain
  network/provider, retry-exhausted marker, or stream/SSE/read-timeout
  messages → 'infra-failed outcome in prompt-run-result->outcome.
- wave-runner-port: 'infra-failed is now a valid terminal outcome kind.
- run-campaign-wave: infra-failed rolls back the begin-attempt!
  increment (status pending, attempt-count restored, current-attempt
  cleared), persists, and stops the campaign with a clear message so
  the user re-runs /go when the provider is healthy. Genuine
  agent/code failures still consume an attempt.

Tests: tests/test-gsd-d8-provider-retry-scaling.rkt (8) — parameter
defaults/adjustability, infra classification (provider/network/
retry-exhausted → infra-failed; contract/tool-loop-limit stay failed),
and run-campaign-wave attempt preservation semantics.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(gsd): D7 — get-base-dir context-type dispatch for planning-read/planning-write (#9356)

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): D7 — get-base-dir context-type dispatch for planning-read/planning-write (#9356)

Campaign 81f9be4b W3 failed 5 attempts. D7 root cause: get-base-dir
(extensions/gsd/tool-handlers.rkt) called ctx-cwd — an extension-ctx
accessor contracted to extension-ctx? — on the tool scheduler's
exec-context struct. Interactive sessions masked the bug because
current-pinned-dir is set after /plan; campaign executors run
reset-all-gsd-state! (pinned-dir #f) so execution reached the broken
call and raised an instant contract violation, burning wave iterations.

Fix: dispatch on the actual context type — exec-context? →
exec-context-working-directory, extension-ctx? → ctx-cwd. Contract on
get-base-dir widened to accept both.

Tests: tests/test-gsd-planning-exec-context.rkt (4) — planning-read and
planning-write under real exec-context with pinned-dir #f (executor
condition), under extension-ctx, and base_dir precedence. RED confirmed
before fix (contract violation reproduced), GREEN after.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix: /go campaign reliability — dispatch watchdog, campaign-aware /retry, executor tool limit, lease owner (D1–D4)

head_commit.message:
fix(runtime,gsd,tui): /go campaign reliability — dispatch watchdog, campaign-aware /retry, executor tool limit, lease owner (D1-D4) (#9351)

D1: tool-dispatch watchdog in runtime/tool-coordinator.rkt — coordinator
phases run on a worker thread with a bounded pre-start deadline
(current-tool-dispatch-timeout-ms, default 60s). If execution never starts
(e.g. a synchronous bus subscriber stalls the first tool.execution.updated
publish — incident 01M05MCKP: 35 dispatches accepted, 34 started, turn open
92 min), emit tool.dispatch.timeout and answer every pending call with a
synthetic error tool-result so the turn recovers. Once started, per-tool
timeouts own the rest.

D2: /retry of a [gsd-planning] EXECUTE prompt now routes through the
extension /go pipeline via ext-command-dispatcher-box (populated in
tui-ctx->cmd-ctx) — full campaign continuation with attempt accounting,
fresh executor sessions, durable state updates, instead of the in-session
plain resubmit that wedged campaign 81f9be4b at the completion boundary.

D3: current-gsd-max-consecutive-tool-calls default 30 -> 100; attempt-3 of
incident W2 died at exactly 30 while the same wave completed with
24-consecutive bursts elsewhere.

D4: campaign lease now records owner session-id + pid (run-campaign! /
execute-campaign-request! / execute-campaign-token! gain #:lease-owner;
TUI, GUI, SDK call sites pass their orchestrating session id) — incident
lock file said owner "unknown".

Tests: tests/test-tool-dispatch-watchdog.rkt (3),
tests/tui/test-retry-campaign-routing.rkt (3), policy floor + lease
owner/pid cases; parameter-inventory entry for the new knob.

head_commit.message:
fix(gsd): /go campaign truth, quarantined gh-wave-finish, reasoning artifact integrity (v1.00.02, #9346)

- /go requires trusted delivery evidence before durable DONE; advisory
  verifier no longer emits contradictory authoritative transitions.
- /go validates git identity via rev-parse; plan errors reported first.
- Campaign waves use fresh isolated sessions; cancellation is wave-owned
  and can no longer shut down global workers.
- gh-wave-finish quarantined: validates required contract (issue_number,
  files, commit_msg, no unknown properties), then fails before mutation.
- Staged-path inspection uses NUL-delimited git diff -z output.
- TUI/GUI terminal effects correlated with active canonical session/turn;
  empty/foreign identities cannot clear active streams or inflate usage.
- Reasoning disclosure uses canonical artifact IDs across Ctrl+O,
  /toggle-detail, and live render; UTF-8 byte-bounded persistence and
  bounded live retention; GUI mutations serialized under gui-state-lock.
- Version 1.00.02; parameter/effect inventories and release docs updated.

Fast gate: 1096 files, 15973/15973 tests passing.
Closes #9346

workflow_runs.name: CI
workflow_runs.display_title: fix/w7 changelog release notes

head_commit.message:
fix(tests): serialize test-test-lint (BUG-0014) + accept 1.x semver

Release CI (run 31918999901) failed at 471b86d7:

1. test-test-lint.rkt ran in the parallel batch (no @isolation
   subprocess / @mutates env tags), so its 'lint-tests.rkt runs'
   subprocess raced with parallel workers compiling test files;
   the lint scan hit a half-written file and crashed (exit 2)
   -> ASSERTION_FAILURE. Flaky in CI, passing standalone.
   classify-filters.rkt mutating-file? (F-7, v0.99.77) treats
   subprocess isolation as serializing; tagging the file moves
   it into the serial batch before any parallel worker starts.

2. test-self-hosting-deep.rkt Deep Test 9 hard-coded 0.x semver
   (>= 0.90); q crossed the 1.00 major line, so the version
   check regex would fail on 1.00.01. Accept 1.x line.

Also dedup the duplicated rationale comment block (botched edit).

head_commit.message:
fix(release): milestone lookup pages state=all; scalar -q reads via gh-text

The close-out milestone stage queried only open milestones via gh-json,
so once v1.00.01 (882) was closed the lookup would fail instead of
reporting the no-op. Paginate state=all (single 100-item page) and read
scalar -q output with a dedicated gh-text helper instead of coercing a
JSON parse of a bare string.

The tool-fail branch of format-entry built a single styled-line and
returned it directly, bypassing wrap-styled-line. Any failure payload
longer than the terminal width was hard-clipped by draw-styled-line!,
hiding exactly the diagnostic tail a user needs. Multi-line errors were
flattened to one unbreakable line first, making stack traces unreadable.

Route the constructed [FAIL] line through the same wrap-styled-line
algorithm the assistant path uses; continuation lines keep the red
style with no repeated prefix, matching the wrapped-assistant
convention. No wrap logic duplicated.

Adds 6 regression tests: 3x-width and narrow-width wrapping, prefix
preservation on the first line, full-payload preservation across
wraps, newline flattening, and short-message passthrough.

v1.00.00-PRE1 W2

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(tui): per-session scrollback path - BUG-0001

head_commit.message:
fix(tui): per-session scrollback path — stop leaking last session's buffer (BUG-0001)

create-tui-session derived scrollback-path from the global session-store
base, so <base>/scrollback.jsonl was shared by every session: each new
session loaded the previous session's transcript on startup, and resume
showed the wrong buffer.

- tui-init.rkt: derive scrollback-path from (agent-session-session-dir
  sess) (in scope at exactly that point); the per-session directory is
  created eagerly by make-agent-session and required by
  resume-agent-session. Also fix the stale create-tui-session contract
  (tui-ctx/agent-session/rt-config/scrollback-path, not the old
  path-string/integer/list/integer signature).
- scrollback.rkt: document the audited save/load lifecycle — load exactly
  once at startup before any buffer exists, save exactly once at exit
  into the session's own file; missing file at load returns '().
- tests: new regression test — session A writes scrollback, new session
  B starts empty (not A's content), resume of A restores A's buffer.

Fixes BUG-0001.
